title: When the Oath Burns Anew
premise: Tamsin Okafor, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Veyra, discovers their name and today's date inscribed in a century-old prophetic text hidden in a smuggler's cache. The book names them as the 'Oathbearer' who must reopen the Last Door — the only passage out of Thornfell, a country erased from maps when the usurper King Aldric annexed it decades ago. Hunted by Aldric's inquisitors and shadowed by Sera, a defector priestess who claims the silent god still listens, Tamsin must choose between the mercenary code that kept them alive and the inheritance of a nation they never knew was theirs. In the end, Tamsin rekindles the god's voice not through duty but through chosen love, burning the old oath to forge a new one, and holds the Door open long enough for the free cities' refugees to escape before collapsing it behind them.
about_author: Gideon Blackwood is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, oaths, and the people who live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin Okafor guides a contraband caravan through the Thornfell passes, establishing their mastery of the mountains and their weary loyalty to a god who stopped answering prayers years ago. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the ache of an unanswered oath.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Memory
chapters.summary: Sheltering in a smuggler's cache, Tamsin finds a leather-bound prophecy written a century ago — and reads their own name beside tonight's date. The final line names them 'Oathbearer of the Last Door.' POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: vertigo, the ground of identity giving way.

chapters.title: What the Inquisitor Burns
chapters.summary: King Aldric's inquisitor, Magistrate Corvel, arrives in the lowland town hunting prophetic texts, leaving ash and informants. Tamsin realizes the book makes them a target. POV: Corvel. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace; Corvel believes he is righteous.

chapters.title: The Defector at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Sera, a former priestess of Veyra, intercepts Tamsin at a ruined shrine, claiming she abandoned Aldric's church after hearing the silent god whisper her name too. She knows what the Last Door is. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Borders That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Fleeing Corvel's riders, Tamsin leads Sera along roads that cross into 'Thornfell' — a country that exists now only in old songs and boundary stones. The land itself seems to remember. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland they never had.

chapters.title: The Toll of Ash Pass
chapters.summary: A toll-gang of exiled Thornfell veterans demands payment; instead of coin, they demand Tamsin recite the old border-oath. Tamsin, half-mocking, does — and the pass lights with ghost-fires. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: belonging offered and feared.

chapters.title: Corvel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvel captures Tamsin's old captain and offers a trade: the prophecy book for the captain's life. Tamsin must decide whether loyalty to comrades outweighs the mission. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: duty as a knife turned inward.

chapters.title: The Book Given Up
chapters.summary: Tamsin surrenders the book to save their captain, then steals it back the same night, burning a bridge — literally — behind them. Sera is furious; the book may be the only map to the Door. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: guilt braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Voices in the Silent God's House
chapters.summary: In Veyra's abandoned mountain temple, Sera prays and something answers — faintly, brokenly, like a voice through deep water. It speaks Tamsin's name. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: terror and hope entangled; faith rekindling against will.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: In the capital, King Aldric learns the Oathbearer lives and orders the Thornfell passes sealed and burned. His advisor warns that the Door, once opened, cannot be closed from either side. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: a tyrant's fear dressed as statecraft.

chapters.title: Blood on the Boundary Stone
chapters.summary: Ambushed on the high road, Tamsin takes a wound that won't close — the old oath is literally failing in their blood. Sera reveals the truth: Tamsin is descended from Thornfell's last royal line. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: betrayal by one's own history.

chapters.title: You Never Told Me
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Sera fracture over secrets — Sera knew the lineage all along and chose the mission over honesty. They part ways at a fork in the pass. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: love against duty, both losing.

chapters.title: The Captain's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's rescued captain, dying of Corvel's torture, confesses she always knew Tamsin's parentage and hid it to keep them free. Her last words release Tamsin from the mercenary band. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: inherited lies forgiven, inherited burden accepted.

chapters.title: Armies in the Passes
chapters.summary: Aldric's armies enter the mountains, torching villages. Refugees flood toward the high country with nowhere to go — except the legend of the Last Door. POV: refugee elder Maren. Emotional beat: collective desperation giving rise to fragile hope.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Burning Wood
chapters.summary: Sera returns, having stolen Corvel's copy of the prophecy, and finds Tamsin leading refugees uphill. Neither apologizes; both begin again. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure — love choosing to stay.

chapters.title: The Price Written Down
chapters.summary: Deciphering the prophecy fully, they learn the Door opens only to an Oathbearer who willingly burns their old oath — renouncing Veyra's protection forever. Outside the Door, there is no god. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: the true cost named aloud.

chapters.title: Corvel at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Corvel corners them at the Door's antechamber, offering Tamsin pardon and rank if they walk away. Tamsin refuses; Corvel, shaken, chooses to arrest rather than kill — his first crack of doubt. POV: Corvel. Emotional beat: an enemy's certainty beginning to burn.

chapters.title: When the Oath Burns Anew
chapters.summary: At the Door itself, Tamsin speaks the renunciation as Aldric's vanguard breaches the antechamber. The old oath ignites — and in its ashes, Veyra's voice returns, not commanding but asking. Tamsin answers freely. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: climax; duty transmuted into chosen devotion.

chapters.title: The Door Held Open
chapters.summary: The Door swings wide onto lands beyond all maps. Tamsin and Sera hold the threshold against Corvel's soldiers while thousands of refugees pour through. Veyra's light shields them; Corvel lowers his sword and steps aside. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: sacrifice suspended between love and loss.

chapters.title: A Country Carried in Exile
chapters.summary: On the far side, the refugees plant Thornfell's boundary stones in new soil. Tamsin, no longer heir to a dead kingdom but citizen of a living one, is asked to lead — and declines, choosing instead to be a road-guide again. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as memory carried forward.

chapters.title: The Door Closed Behind Them
chapters.summary: Tamsin speaks the closing words, sealing the Door so Aldric can never follow. The silence afterward is not the god's absence but a held breath. Sera takes their hand. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: grief and peace in the same exhale.

chapters.title: Every Road Forward
chapters.summary: Seasons later, Tamsin guides the first caravan through the new country's unmarked passes, the prophecy book repurposed as a road ledger. Somewhere ahead, Veyra's shrines are being built again — small ones, with open doors. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: resolution; belonging found not in blood or oath, but in the walking.
